suggestions.title: First inbound FK on `step` (ON DELETE CASCADE) means any future drizzle table-recreate of `step` silently wipes every gate_verdict row
suggestions.evidence: 0044_merge_gate_tables.sql:51 `FOREIGN KEY (stepId) REFERENCES step(id) ... ON DELETE cascade`. drizzle-orm 0.45.2 sqlite-core/dialect.js:657 runs every pending migration inside `BEGIN ... COMMIT`, and SQLite ignores `PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF` inside a transaction. With FKs on, `DROP TABLE step` performs an implicit DELETE that fires cascades. The repo has recreated `step` before (0004_opposite_chimera.sql:16-34, __new_step / DROP TABLE step). Probe on the head's migrations: insert a step and a verdict, then apply a drizzle-shaped 0045 that recreates step. Result: step 1 row kept, gate_verdict 0 rows. Nothing references step.id before this PR, and step.buildId deliberately has no FK.
suggestions.failurePath: Once S5a writes verdicts, a later schema change to `step` that drizzle-kit emits as a table recreate (a new NOT NULL constraint, a changed default, an added FK) runs at server boot. It deletes all gate_verdict rows while the step rows are copied back, with no error. Readiness then loses every verdict, including `verify` verdicts with outcome `tampered`. S2 (#1421 readiness.ts) treats those as permanent for the whole build, across digests. After the wipe, a later verify pass on the current digest clears a gate that should have stayed blocked. A `build` recreate has the same effect on all four tables; plan and branch_sync already carry that pre-existing hazard. Options: drop the step FK and rely on the buildId cascade (stepId is minted by the server); add a test that fails when any migration after the gate migration contains `DROP TABLE \`step\`` or `DROP TABLE \`build\``; or document that recreates of these tables must preserve gate rows.

suggestions.title: F1 upgrade test runs the head's seed() against a pre-gate database, so a later column added to user/team breaks it
suggestions.evidence: The test migrates a copy of the journal cut before the gate migration (line 229), then calls `seed(oldDb)` with the head's drizzle schema. seed.ts runs `db.select().from(team)` and `db.select().from(user)`, which list every column in the head schema explicitly. The test aims to survive renumbering and later migrations (F16: it finds the migration by content and compares `when` against every earlier entry).
suggestions.failurePath: Suppose a later PR adds a column to `team` or `user` in a migration after the gate migration. The pre-gate DB lacks that column, so `seed(oldDb)` throws 'no such column' and the upgrade test fails even though the gate migration still applies correctly. Seeding the old DB's team row with raw SQL, as seedBuild already does for project/todo/build/step, removes the dependency on head-schema columns.

suggestions.title: One-line helper readJournal has a single call site and is not inlined

The rule is broken as written, with no runtime effect.

Findings: none." There is no /simplify entry in gates-s3.txt or in the PR's Verified section.

suggestions.title: No test pins NOT NULL on gate_verdict.expectedHeadSha or gate_round.patchDigest; making either nullable survives the whole suite
suggestions.failurePath: Mutation 1: in schema.ts, make gateVerdict.expectedHeadSha nullable and regenerate the migration. verdictRow (line 115) always sets expectedHeadSha to H1, and F8 (line 323) sets only patchDigest, headSha and perspective to null, so all 20 tests stay green. The property the PR states (a verdict always carries the head the server pinned at dispatch, so a step with no pinned head gets no verdict row) then goes unenforced, and S5a could store unbindable verdicts without any test noticing. Mutation 2: make gate_round.patchDigest nullable. SQLite UNIQUE treats NULLs as distinct, so two rounds with a null digest on one build both insert and the F2 guarantee of one round per patch is bypassed. F2 (line 255) only inserts non-null digests, so it stays green. Neither mutation is in s3-mutations.txt. One negative insert per column (null expectedHeadSha throws NOT NULL; null round patchDigest throws NOT NULL) would pin both.

suggestions.title: F15 is a textual tripwire that already passes on main and stays green if the machine path writes verdicts through a helper
suggestions.failurePath: The test regex-scans only routes-machine.ts and services/machine*.ts for the literal table or export names. Suppose a later segment has machines.ts (for example the step-done report that routes-machine.ts:380 feeds) call a function in services/merge-gate/*.ts or builds.ts that inserts into gate_verdict from machine-supplied fields. No scanned file then mentions gate_verdict or gateVerdict, so F15 stays green while plan fact 1 (verdicts must not come from data a machine can forge) is broken. The PR openly says the test passes on main and guards nothing yet. It is not proof for fact 1; the real guard has to come with S5a's writer (a behavioural test that a transcript or done upload cannot create or overwrite a gate_verdict row).

suggestions.title: Verdict rows are deleted along with their step (ON DELETE CASCADE on gate_verdict.stepId)
suggestions.failurePath: Today every code path that deletes a step also deletes its build (projects.ts:102, todos.ts:689/731), so no failure exists at this head. In a later segment, any step delete or replace that keeps the build (a retry or a cleanup, for example) would silently remove that step's gate_verdict. A recorded 'block' or 'tampered' verdict would then stop counting, and readiness could turn ready without a new review. When the S5a, S6a or S7 writers land, they should either never delete review, verify or decision steps while their build lives, or treat a step whose verdict is missing as unresolved rather than passing.
suggestions.evidence: gate_verdict.stepId .references(() => step.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' }) at schema.ts, and FOREIGN KEY (`stepId`) REFERENCES `step`(`id`) ... ON DELETE cascade in 0044_merge_gate_tables.sql:51. The mutation file s3-mutations.txt pins the cascade as intended.

suggestions.title: Gate value lists in schema.ts are type-only and sit outside the D4 category-4 gate-source paths
suggestions.failurePath: GateVerdictOutcome, GatePolicy, GateRoundState and the blocker class are TypeScript `$type` literals with no CHECK constraint. Editing them produces no migration, so no path under drizzle/** changes. They live in apps/server/src/db/schema.ts, which is in D4's auto-mergeable set rather than in the category-4 locations (services/merge-gate/**, records/merge-gate.ts, daemon merge-decision.ts). A later PR that changes only these literals would therefore not be forced to human review by name. The impact is limited because the database enforces nothing either way, and the runtime gate logic lives in the protected paths. Consider importing the S1 and S2 types once they merge, so that the value lists have a single source under category 4.
suggestions.evidence: schema.ts lines 771-801: the comments say the literals are copied from S1/S2 and not imported, and that value ranges deliberately have no CHECK constraint. ADR 0021 D4 category 4 says new gate source must not be placed elsewhere.
